London, 22<sup>nd</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Chrysler LLC’s** lenders have offered to take equity in a restructured automaker allied with Fiat SpA in exchange for writing off about 35% of the $7 billion they are owed, according to people familiar with the closed-door talks.  Under the terms of the counter-offer conveyed to the U.S. Treasury on Monday, the lenders would retain about $4.5 billion in debt and take a stake of more than a third of a new Chrysler supported by new U.S. government investment and a ground-breaking deal with Fiat.  That would mark a much richer payout than U.S. officials first offered the banks that helped finance Chrysler’s 2007 sale to private equity firm Cerberus Capital Management LP.  The gap underscores the tension between a diverse group of creditors, including more aggressive funds, and the government officials dictating turnaround terms for Chrysler with just nine days before a deadline for the automaker to complete its restructuring talks.  Rep. Gary Peters called the counter-offer “an affront to taxpayers…These debt holders were offered fair market value for the debt, and the banks have responded by asking for a windfall.”  The Obama administration’s autos task force had proposed that creditors write off $6 billion of what they are owed, a proposal that would have left the group of institutional creditors holding about $1 billion in Chrysler debt. That would represent a write-down of 85% of the loan value.  The Chrysler counter-offer including equity would allow the roughly 45 banks and funds that hold Chrysler debt to benefit from investment gains if it succeeds in a restructuring that could see operational control shift to Fiat CEO Sergio Marchionne. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**The Obama administration** will make about $500 million available to Chrysler LLC through the end of this month as it seeks to reach an alliance with Fiat, and up to $5 billion through May to help GM restructure outside of bankruptcy. Separately, the United Auto Workers union urged its members to lobby the White House to ensure that workers and retirees are treated fairly in negotiations on new concessions. _Source:  Reuters_ 

**Honda Motor Co** President Takeo Fukui said on Tuesday the U.S. market has shown signs of having bottomed out since the start of April.  Honda, the No. 2 Japanese carmaker, and GS Yuasa Corp, Asia’s biggest car battery maker, said they planned to make lithium-ion batteries for hybrid cars from 2010 at a plant in Kyoto.  Blue Energy Co, in which battery maker GS Yuasa holds a 51 percent and Honda the remainder, will spend 25 billion yen ($255 million) to build the plant. The plant will have the capacity to supply batteries for 200,000 to 300,000 hybrid cars a year. _Source:  The Guardian_ 

**Aquarius Platinum** reported a net profit of $6,5-million for Q1 09, compared to the net losses of $48,6million and $21,5-million achieved in the previous two quarters.   Production was d

own to 97 212 oz of PGMs (4E), compared with the 131 843 oz of PGMs 4E produced in the previous quarter. The temporary suspension of operations at the subsidence-hit Everest mine lead to a loss of production of 30 000 oz of PGMs in the quarter.  During the quarter, the group had continued to focus on reducing its unit costs. It had already seen a 30% reduction in unit costs in the 2009 financial year, of which 10% was attributable to a reduction of the rand cost base and the remaining 20% was attributable to the US dollar’s strength against the rand.  Unit costs at the Mimosa mine, in Zimbabwe, had, however, increased as a result of the dollarisation of the Zimbabwean economy.  In South Africa, diesel costs had come down by 29,6% in the third quarter, explosives costs were down 10,45% and steel costs were down 7,9%. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Global TFT-LCD panel shipments** in Q2 09 are estimated to increase by 30% on a quarterly basis due to growing demand, according to industry sources.  The industry’s utilization rates rose from 50% in January to 62% in February, and to nearly 70% in March. _Source:  Digitimes_
